How can we smell dangerous natural gas leaks if it has no smell?

Utility companies add a chemical called mercaptan! This gives the odorless natural gas a smell so you can detect leaks.

Paano natin maamoy ang delikadong tagas ng natural gas kung wala naman itong amoy?

Nagdadagdag ang mga utility company ng chemical na tinatawag na mercaptan! Binibigyan nito ng amoy ang natural gas para maamoy mo ang tagas.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato pag-amoy ang delikado nga leak sa natural gas kung wala man kini baho?

Ang mga utility company mag‑butang og chemical nga gitawag ug mercaptan! Hatagan niini og baho ang natural gas aron maamoy nimo ang leak.

copy.en:
How many times do we blink a day?

We blink about 15 to 20 times every minute, that adds up to around 28,000 blinks in one day!
copy.tl:
Ilang beses tayo kumukurap sa isang araw?

Kumukurap tayo ng halos 15 hanggang 20 beses bawat minuto, umaabot ito ng humigit-kumulang 28,000 beses sa isang araw!
copy.bis:
Pilay ka beses ta mokirok sa usa ka adlaw?

Mokirok kita og mga 15 hangtod 20 ka beses matag minuto, mokabat kini og gibana-bana nga 28,000 ka beses sa usa ka adlaw!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the retina, a part of the eye, and its function in sensing light. It does not address the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) at all.

copy.en:
What is the retina?

The retina is a special layer at the back of your eye. It senses light so your brain can turn it into what you see.
copy.tl:
Ano ang retina?

Ang retina ay ang espesyal na bahagi sa likod ng mata. Ito ang nakakakita ng liwanag para maproseso ng utak kung ano ang nakikita mo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang retina?

Ang retina mao ang pinasahi nga bahin sa likod sa mata. Kini ang makadetect sa kahayag aron maproseso sa utok ang imong nakita.

Nagpapakita ito ng high optical transparency, isang physical property na nagpapahintulot ng deep light penetration!
copy.bis:
Ngano klaro ang tubig sa Hinatuan Enchanted River?

Nagpakita kini og high optical transparency, usa ka physical property nga nagtugot sa deep light penetration!

copy.en:
Did you know rocks can release gas?

Uranium in rocks and soil releases radon gas, which can cause lung cancer when inhaled indoors.
copy.tl:
Alam mo bang may gas ang mga bato?

Ang uranium sa bato at lupa ay naglalabas ng radon gas na nakakadulot ng lung cancer kapag na-inhale sa loob ng bahay.
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga naay gas ang mga bato?

Ang uranium sa bato ug yuta nagpagawas og radon gas nga makapahimo og lung cancer kung gininhawa sa sulod sa balay.

How heavy are the parts of a water molecule?

A water molecule has one oxygen atom that weighs eight times more than the two combined hydrogen atoms!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabigat ang mga parts ng water molecule?

Ang isang water molecule ay may isang oxygen atom na walong beses mas mabigat kaysa sa dalawang hydrogen atoms!
copy.bis:
Gaano kabug-at ang mga parts sa water molecule?

Ang usa ka water molecule adunay usa ka oxygen atom nga 8 ka beses mas bug-at kaysa sa duha ka hydrogen atoms!

copy.bis: Ang gamma rays kay highly penetrating waves, nagpasabot nga makalusot sila sa daghang materyales, mao nga mainampingon silang gigamit sa mga medikal nga pagtambal.

copy.tl: Ang mga gas sa loob ng magma chamber, tulad ng water vapor at carbon dioxide, ay lumalaki habang tumataas ang temperature, at ang paglaki na ito ang nagpapataas ng pressure na maaaring mag-trigger ng eruption.
copy.bis: Ang mga gas sa sulod sa magma chamber, sama sa water vapor ug carbon dioxide, molapad samtang mosaka ang temperature, ug kini nga paglapad maoy nagpataas sa pressure nga mahimong mag-trigger sa eruption.

copy.tl: Ang gathering data ay nangangahulugang gumawa ng paghuhusga batay sa resulta ng eksperimento, kaya maingat na tinitingnan ng scientist kung ano talaga ang nangyari.
copy.bis: Ang gathering data nagpasabot sa paghimo og paghukom base sa resulta sa eksperimento, mao nga ang scientist nagtan-aw pag-ayo kon unsa gyud ang nahitabo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about rainy-day clothing and staying dry, with no mention of cells, unicellular/multicellular organisms, bacteria, or humans as multicellular organisms. It does not support the competency in any way.

Ever wonder how cars shift gears in such a tiny space?

A planetary gear set uses a sun gear, planet gears, and a ring gear to give many gear ratios in a small package — just like in automatic transmissions!
copy.tl:
Naisip mo ba kung paano nagpapalit ng gear ang sasakyan sa maliit na espasyo?

Ang planetary gear set ay gumagamit ng sun gear, planet gears, at ring gear para magbigay ng maraming gear ratio sa maliit na espasyo — tulad ng sa automatic transmissions!
copy.bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo unsaon pagbalhin sa gear sa sakyanan sa gamay nga lugar?

Ang planetary gear set naggamit sa sun gear, planet gears, ug ring gear aron makahatag og daghang gear ratio sa gamay nga pakete — sama sa automatic transmissions!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The gene pool is the total genetic composition of all individuals in a population
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the gene pool and evolution, which is genetics/evolution content. G5-E-4 requires explaining how soil is formed from rocks and minerals. There is no connection to soil, rocks, or minerals.

copy.en:
What do scientists mean when they say a population's gene pool changed?

The gene pool is the total genetic composition of all individuals in a population, and evolution is a change in that gene pool!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ibig sabihin ng mga siyentista kapag sinabi nilang nagbago ang gene pool ng isang population?

Ang gene pool ay ang kabuuang genetic composition ng lahat ng indibidwal sa isang population, at ang evolution ay pagbabago sa gene pool na iyon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buot ipasabot sa mga siyentista kon moingon sila nga nausab ang gene pool sa usa ka population?

Ang gene pool mao ang kinatibuk-ang genetic composition sa tanang indibidwal sa usa ka population, ug ang evolution mao ang pagbag-o sa maong gene pool!

copy.tl: Sa mga cross ni Mendel, ang P1 ay ang parent generation, ang F1 ay ang unang filial na anak, at ang F2 ay ang pangalawang filial na anak.
copy.bis: Sa mga cross ni Mendel, ang P1 mao ang parent generation, ang F1 mao ang unang filial nga anak, ug ang F2 mao ang ikaduhang filial nga anak.

copy.tl: Ang genes ay maliliit na bahagi sa loob ng cells na nakakaapekto sa paglaki ng isang bata, tulad ng kung magkakaroon siya ng kulot o tuwid na buhok.
copy.bis: Ang genes kay gagmay nga mga parte sa sulod sa cells nga makaapekto sa pagtubo sa bata, sama sa kung kulot ba o tul-id ang iyang buhok.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses genus and species, not plant adaptations to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. Unrelated to this competency.

copy.en:
What is the difference between a genus and a species?

A genus is a larger group that contains closely related species. For example, Panthera is the genus that includes both lions and tigers.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng genus at species?

Ang genus ay mas malaking grupo na naglalaman ng mga species na malapit na magkakaugnay. Halimbawa, ang Panthera ay genus na kinabibilangan ng parehong leon at tigre.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang kalainan tali sa genus ug species?

Ang genus usa ka mas dako nga grupo nga adunay mga species nga suod og relasyon. Pananglitan, ang Panthera mao ang genus nga naglakip sa leon ug tigre.

copy.tl: Gumagamit ang mga geologist ng parehong relative at absolute dating upang mabuo ang geologic time scale, na naghahati sa 4.6-bilyong taong kasaysayan ng Daigdig sa mga eon, era, at period.
copy.bis: Ang mga geologist mogamit sa duha ka relative ug absolute dating aron matukod ang geologic time scale, nga nagbahin sa 4.6-bilyones ka tuig nga kasaysayan sa Yuta ngadto sa mga eon, era, ug period.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about germ transmission and hand hygiene, not about how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. It does not support the competency's content.

copy.en: Germs spread easily from dirty hands to your mouth, eyes, and food — that's why keeping your hands clean matters.
copy.tl: Madaling kumakalat ang mikrobyo mula sa maruming kamay patungo sa bibig, mata, at pagkain, kaya mahalaga ang paglilinis.
copy.bis: Ang mikrobyo dali rang mokaylap gikan sa hugaw nga kamot ngadto sa baba, mata, ug pagkaon, mao nga importante ang pagpakalimpyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The eyes, nose, and mouth are like doorways where germs enter your body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how germs enter through the eyes, nose, and mouth, but does not describe how any of the listed body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. It is about infection transmission, not system function.

copy.en:
Why is touching your face risky?

The eyes, nose, and mouth are like doorways where germs enter your body. Germs on your hand can't make you sick until you touch your face.
copy.tl:
Bakit mapanganib ang paghawak ng mukha?

Ang mata, ilong, at bibig ay parang pintuan kung saan pumapasok ang germs sa katawan. Kahit may germs sa kamay mo, hindi ka agad magkakasakit kung hindi mo hahawakan ang mukha mo.
copy.bis:
Nganong peligroso ang paghikap sa nawong?

Ang mata, ilong, ug baba sama sa mga pultahan diin mosulod ang germs sa lawas. Bisan adunay germs sa imong kamot, dili ka dayon masakit kon dili nimo hikapon ang imong nawong.

assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about describing science process skills (observing, predicting, measuring) using units like millimeter, centimeter, and meter. copy.en: The symbol for the prefix "giga" is a capital "G"! Always use the big letter!
copy.tl: Ang simbolo para sa unlaping "giga" ay malaking "G"! Palaging gamitin ang malaking letra!
copy.bis: Ang simbolo para sa prefix nga "giga" kay dako nga "G"! Kanunay gamita ang dako nga letra!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the shoulder and pelvic girdles anchoring limbs, which is skeletal anatomy. G4-M-3 is about chemical properties of materials (burning, reactivity, degradability). No overlap in subject matter.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass

copy.en: The shoulder girdle connects your arms to your body, and the pelvic girdle connects your legs to your body, anchoring your limbs.
copy.tl: Ang shoulder girdle ang nagdudugtong ng braso sa katawan, at ang pelvic girdle ang nagdudugtong ng binti sa katawan, na nagsisilbing angkla ng mga limbs.
copy.bis: Ang shoulder girdle mao ang nagdugtong sa bukton sa lawas, ug ang pelvic girdle mao ang nagdugtong sa batiis sa lawas, nga nagsilbing angkla sa mga limbs.

copy.en: Fossils of the plant Glossopteris are found in rocks across South America, Africa, India, Australia, and Antarctica, showing these lands were once connected.
copy.tl: Ang mga fossil ng halamang Glossopteris ay matatagpuan sa mga bato sa South America, Africa, India, Australia, at Antarctica, na nagpapakitang dating magkakadikit ang mga lupaing ito.
copy.bis: Ang mga fossil sa tanom nga Glossopteris makita sa mga bato sa South America, Africa, India, Australia, ug Antarctica, nga nagpakita nga kaniadto nagkahiusa kini nga mga yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both start with glycolysis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: examine a local weather chart to make simple interpretations about the local weather and describe and practice safety precautions to use during poor or extreme weather conditions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the shared first step of lactic acid and alcoholic fermentation (glycolysis). It contains no information about weather charts, local weather interpretation, or safety precautions for poor/extreme weather, which are the focus of G4-E-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Both start with glycolysis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about fermentation and glycolysis, not about weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. There is no connection to the competency's subject matter.

copy.en:
What step do both lactic acid and alcoholic fermentation share?

Both start with glycolysis, the splitting of a glucose sugar molecule into two smaller pyruvate molecules, releasing a little energy.
copy.tl:
Anong hakbang ang pareho sa lactic acid at alcoholic fermentation?

Pareho silang nagsisimula sa glycolysis, ang paghahati ng isang glucose sugar molecule sa dalawang mas maliit na pyruvate molecule, na naglalabas ng kaunting enerhiya.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga lakang ang pareho sa lactic acid ug alcoholic fermentation?

Pareho silang magsugod sa glycolysis, ang pagbahin sa usa ka glucose sugar molecule ngadto sa duha ka mas gamay nga pyruvate molecule, nga nagpagawas ug gamay nga enerhiya.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Goiter is an abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses goiter and thyroid hormone production, with no mention of any scientist or invention. It does not support the competency of identifying a famous scientist and their invention/s.

copy.en:
Why does the thyroid gland sometimes swell?

Goiter is an abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, often caused by too little or too much thyroid hormone production.
copy.tl:
Bakit minsan namamaga ang thyroid gland?

Ang goiter ay abnormal na paglaki ng thyroid gland, kadalasang sanhi ng kulang o sobrang paggawa ng thyroid hormones.
copy.bis:
Ngano usahay mohubag man ang thyroid gland?

Ang goiter usa ka abnormal nga pagdako sa thyroid gland, sagad tungod sa kulang o sobra nga paghimo ug thyroid hormones.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why does the volume-temperature graph pass through the origin?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to describe and explain what mechanisms that drive the movement of tectonic plates including the role of the asthenosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the volume-temperature relationship of a gas at absolute zero (Charles's law / absolute zero concept). G10-E-5 is about mechanisms driving tectonic plate movement and the role of the asthenosphere. There is no connection to plate tectonics, Earth's interior, or the asthenosphere.

copy.en:
Why does the volume-temperature graph pass through the origin?

Because at zero Kelvin, the volume of a gas would theoretically be zero, so the line starts at the point (0,0).
copy.tl:
Bakit dumadaan sa origin ang graph ng volume-temperature?

Dahil sa zero Kelvin, ang volume ng gas ay theoretically magiging zero, kaya nagsisimula ang linya sa punto na (0,0).
copy.bis:
Ngano moagi man sa origin ang graph sa volume-temperature?

Kay sa zero Kelvin, ang volume sa gas theoretically mahimong zero, mao nga magsugod ang linya sa punto nga (0,0).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Frederick Griffith discovered in 1928
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Griffith's bacterial transformation experiment, which is a biology/genetics topic. It has no relation to sources of light or their uses, which is the subject of G3-F-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Frederick Griffith discovered in 1928
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about bacterial transformation, not about sources and uses of light, sound, or heat energy. It does not support G4-F-10 in any way.

copy.en: Frederick Griffith discovered in 1928 that a factor in diseased bacteria can transform harmless bacteria into deadly bacteria.
copy.tl: Natuklasan ni Frederick Griffith noong 1928 na may factor sa diseased bacteria na kayang gawing deadly bacteria ang harmless bacteria.
copy.bis: Nadiskobrehan ni Frederick Griffith sa 1928 nga adunay factor sa diseased bacteria nga makahimo sa harmless bacteria nga mahimong deadly bacteria.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vertical columns in the periodic table are called groups or families
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches periodic table groups and valence electrons, which is a chemistry topic unrelated to the G4-M-3 competency about chemical properties of materials (burning, reactivity, degradability). No instructional support for the assigned competency.

copy.en: Vertical columns in the periodic table are called groups or families, and the group number tells you how many valence electrons, or outermost electrons, an element has.
copy.tl: Ang mga patayong hanay sa periodic table ay tinatawag na groups o families, at sinasabi ng group number kung ilang valence electrons, o pinakalabas na electrons, mayroon ang isang elemento.
copy.bis: Ang mga pinatindog nga laray sa periodic table gitawag ug groups o families, ug ang group number nagsulti kanimo kung pila ka valence electrons, o pinakagawas nga electrons, ang naa sa usa ka elemento.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Gutenberg Bible was actually one of the very first books printed using movable type!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires identifying a famous scientist and their invention. The card discusses the Gutenberg Bible as an early printed book and mentions movable type, but it does not identify a scientist (Gutenberg is not named) or describe an invention as a scientific contribution. The content does not support the skill of identifying a scientist and their invention.

copy.en:
What was one of the very first books printed using movable type?

The Gutenberg Bible was actually one of the very first books printed using movable type!
copy.tl:
Ano ang isa sa mga unang aklat na inimprenta gamit ang movable type?

Ang Gutenberg Bible ang isa sa unang mga aklat na inimprenta gamit ang movable type!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang usa sa mga unang libro nga giimprenta gamit ang movable type?

Ang Gutenberg Bible maoy usa sa unang mga libro nga giimprenta gamit ang movable type!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's the deepest ocean layer! You can find it inside deep trenches from about 6,000 meters down.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks students to identify local examples of landforms and bodies of water (mountains, valleys, rivers, coastlines) and describe their influence on living and non-living components. The card describes the hadal zone, a deep-ocean depth layer in trenches, which is not a local landform or body of water example and does not address influence on the environment. It is unrelated to the competency's subject.

copy.en:
What is the hadal zone?

It's the deepest ocean layer! You can find it inside deep trenches from about 6,000 meters down.
copy.tl:
Ano ang hadal zone?

Ito ang pinakamalalim na sona ng karagatan! Matatagpuan ito sa mga malalalim na kanal mula mga 6,000 metro pababa.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang hadal zone?

Mao kini ang pinakalawom nga sona sa dagat! Makit-an kini sulod sa lawom nga mga kanal gikan sa mga 6,000 ka metro paubos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mirror about half your height is enough to see your full body image from head to toe.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the optics of a plane mirror (half-height mirror for full-body view), which is unrelated to assembling or drawing a simple electrical circuit with batteries, wires, switch, and bulb/motor/buzzer. The format-required activity (assembled/drawn simple circuit) is also absent.

copy.en:
Do you need a mirror as tall as you to see your whole body?

No! A mirror about half your height is enough to see your full body image from head to toe.
copy.tl:
Kailangan mo ba ng salamin na kasing tangkad mo para makita ang buong katawan mo?

Hindi! Ang salamin na halos kalahati ng tangkad mo ay sapat na para makita ang buong imahe mo mula ulo hanggang paa.
copy.bis:
Kinahanglan ba nimo og samin nga sama ka taas nimo aron makita ang tibuok lawas?

Dili! Ang samin nga mga katunga sa imong gitas-on igo na aron makita ang tibuok imahe nimo gikan ulo hangtod tiil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Halogens like fluorine and chlorine are nonmetals that are very reactive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses chemical reactivity of halogens, not changes of state or particle arrangement/energy changes. It provides no instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Halogens like fluorine and chlorine are nonmetals that are very reactive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about halogen reactivity, not about particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects. It does not support the particle model competency.

copy.en: Halogens like fluorine and chlorine are nonmetals that are very reactive, meaning they easily combine with other elements.
copy.tl: Ang halogens tulad ng fluorine at chlorine ay mga nonmetal na napaka-reactive, ibig sabihin madali silang sumama sa ibang element.
copy.bis: Ang halogens sama sa fluorine ug chlorine mga nonmetal nga reactive kaayo, nagpasabot nga dali silang mosagol sa laing element.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Germs stick to and spread from wet hands more easily than dry ones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify issues and concerns in the local community and how they could be addressed by science, such as the treatment of waste
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about hand hygiene and drying hands, not about identifying local community issues/concerns or how science addresses them, such as waste treatment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Germs stick to and spread from wet hands more easily than dry ones
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not address basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter); it is about hand drying and germ spread.

copy.en: Germs stick to and spread from wet hands more easily than dry ones, so it's important to dry your hands with a clean towel or tissue after washing.
copy.tl: Mas madaling dumikit at kumalat ang germs sa basang kamay kaysa sa tuyo, kaya mahalagang patuyuin ang kamay gamit ang malinis na tuwalya o tissue pagkahugas.
copy.bis: Mas dali mopilit ug mokaylap ang germs sa basa nga kamot kaysa sa uga, mao nga importante nga pauga-on ang kamot gamit limpyo nga tuwalya o tissue human manghugas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The hanging wall is the block of rock that sits above the fault plane, while the footwall is the block below it.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines geological fault terms (hanging wall, footwall) and has no connection to simple machines (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys) or their advantages/limitations. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en:
What are the hanging wall and footwall?

They are the two blocks of rock on either side of a fault. The hanging wall is the block above the fault line, and the footwall is the block below it.
copy.tl:
Ano ang hanging wall at footwall?

Ang mga ito ay ang dalawang bloke ng bato sa magkabilang gilid ng isang fault. Ang hanging wall ay ang bloke sa itaas ng fault line, at ang footwall ay ang bloke sa ilalim nito.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang hanging wall ug footwall?

Kini sila ang duha ka bloke sa bato sa matag kilid sa usa ka fault. Ang hanging wall mao ang bloke sa taas sa fault line, ug ang footwall mao ang bloke sa ilawom niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solid particles are held by strong attractive forces, so solids are difficult to compress.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why solids are hard to compress using the particle model. G7-M-8 is about identifying the role of solute and solvent in a solution, which is unrelated to particle arrangement or compressibility of solids.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solid particles are held by strong attractive forces, so solids are difficult to compress.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes solid particle behavior, not uniform or non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. G6-M-4 concerns mixtures, not the compressibility of pure solids.

copy.en: Solid particles are held by strong attractive forces, so solids are difficult to compress.
copy.tl: Ang mga particles ng solid ay hawak ng malakas na attractive forces, kaya mahirap i-compress ang solid.
copy.bis: Ang mga particles sa solid gigunitan sa kusog nga attractive forces, mao nga lisod i-compress ang solid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pieces of broken glass are harmful waste because their sharp edges can cut skin and cause serious injuries.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses broken glass as harmful waste and its injury risk, which has no connection to earthquakes, their magnitude, or community effects. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Pieces of broken glass are harmful waste because their sharp edges can cut skin and cause serious injuries.
copy.tl: Ang mga piraso ng basag na salamin ay harmful waste dahil ang matatalim na gilid nito ay maaaring makasugat ng balat at magdulot ng malubhang pinsala.
copy.bis: Ang mga piraso sa nabuak nga baso kay harmful waste tungod kay ang hait nga mga kilid niini makasamad sa panit ug makapahinabog grabe nga kadaot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: seafloor spreading theory
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Harry Hess's seafloor spreading theory, a geological concept about continental drift. It has no content about observing or describing celestial objects in the sky (Sun, Moon, planets, stars), so it does not support this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: seafloor spreading theory
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about seafloor spreading and continental drift, not about a Sun-Earth-Moon system model, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses. It provides no instructional support for this competency.

copy.en: In 1960, American geophysicist Harry Hess proposed the seafloor spreading theory, explaining that drifting continents were caused by the spreading of the seafloor.
copy.tl: Noong 1960, iminungkahi ng American geophysicist na si Harry Hess ang seafloor spreading theory, na nagpapaliwanag na ang pag-anod ng mga kontinente ay sanhi ng pagkalat ng seafloor.
copy.bis: Niadtong 1960, gisugyot sa American geophysicist nga si Harry Hess ang seafloor spreading theory, nga nagpasabot nga ang pag-anod sa mga kontinente gipahinabo sa pagkatag sa seafloor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: No, they are hazardous materials. This means they can harm your health if you touch, smell, or drink them!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Household chemical safety is unrelated to plant reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: rubbing alcohol and insecticides
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: Hazardous household chemicals are not specialized plant structures.

copy.en:
Are rubbing alcohol and insecticides safe to play with?

No, they are hazardous materials. This means they can harm your health if you touch, smell, or drink them!
copy.tl:
Ligtas bang paglaruan ang rubbing alcohol at insecticides?

Hindi, ang mga ito ay hazardous materials. Ibig sabihin, maaari itong makasama sa iyong kalusugan kapag hinawakan, naamoy, o nainom!
copy.bis:
Luwas ba nga dulaan ang rubbing alcohol ug insecticides?

Dili, kini mga hazardous materials. Nagpasabot nga makadaot kini sa imong panglawas kung hikapon, simhuton, o imnon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Healthy habits protect the sense organs from diseases
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how global climatic phenomena, such as the El Niño Southern Oscillation, may impact weather systems
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses personal hygiene and diet for sense organs, which is unrelated to global climatic phenomena such as El Niño Southern Oscillation and their impact on weather systems.

copy.en: Healthy habits protect the sense organs from diseases, so we must keep them clean and eat a balanced diet.
copy.tl: Ang mga healthy habits ay nagpoprotekta sa mga sense organs mula sa mga sakit, kaya dapat natin itong panatilihing malinis at kumain ng balanced diet.
copy.bis: Ang mga healthy habits nagprotektar sa mga sense organs batok sa mga sakit, busa kinahanglan nato kining huptan nga limpyo ug mokaon ug balanced diet.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The heart is one organ that belongs to the circulatory system
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: apply the features of a fair test: a. change one factor, b. measure one factor, and c. keep all other factors the same
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that the heart is an organ belonging to the circulatory system. It contains no content about fair tests, changing one factor, measuring one factor, or keeping other factors the same. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's subject.

copy.en:
Is my heart an organ or an organ system?

It is an organ! The heart is one organ that belongs to the circulatory system, which also includes veins and arteries.
copy.tl:
Ang puso ko ba ay isang organ o isang organ system?

Ito ay isang organ! Ang puso ay isang organ na kabilang sa circulatory system, na kasama rin ang veins at arteries.
copy.bis:
Ang akong kasingkasing usa ba ka organ o usa ka organ system?

Kini usa ka organ! Ang kasingkasing usa ka organ nga sakop sa circulatory system, nga naglakip usab sa veins ug arteries.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Matter can change its physical form when heated or cooled
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes physical changes of state (melting, freezing, etc.), not the properties of pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements/compounds, or unique proton numbers. No instructional support for G8-M-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Matter can change its physical form when heated or cooled
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical name of some common covalent compounds, including water (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and ammonia (NH3)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about physical changes of state, not writing chemical formulas or names of covalent compounds such as water, carbon dioxide, or ammonia. Unrelated to G9-M-8.

copy.en: Matter can change its physical form when heated or cooled, and these changes include melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, and deposition.
copy.tl: Ang matter ay maaaring magbago ng pisikal na anyo kapag naiinitan o nalalamigan, at kabilang sa mga pagbabagong ito ang melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, at deposition.
copy.bis: Ang matter mahimong mag-usab sa pisikal nga porma kung initan o pabugnawan, ug apil sa mga pagbag-o kini ang melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation, ug deposition.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heat cannot be wholly transformed into work
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses thermodynamics (heat-to-work conversion), which is unrelated to observing and describing animal outer body parts and their roles in movement and feeding. The assigned competency is for Grade 3 Living Things, while the card content is physics.

copy.en: In general, heat cannot be wholly transformed into work because thermal energy, when converted, is mostly dissipated into the system as wasted energy.
copy.tl: Sa pangkalahatan, ang heat ay hindi maaaring ganap na maging work dahil ang thermal energy, kapag na-convert, ay kadalasang nawawala sa system bilang nasasayang na energy.
copy.bis: Sa kinatibuk-an, ang heat dili hingpit nga mahimong work tungod kay ang thermal energy, kung ma-convert, kasagarang mawala sa system isip nausik nga energy.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heat, air, light, and moisture can damage medicines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how heat, air, light, and moisture damage medicines. G5-F-10 requires making a simple electromagnet and observing/recording its properties. There is no connection to electromagnets, electricity, or magnetism; the card is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Heat, air, light, and moisture can damage medicines and make them less effective or unsafe to take.
copy.tl: Ang init, hangin, liwanag, at moisture ay maaaring makasira ng mga gamot at gawin itong hindi gaanong epektibo o hindi ligtas inumin.
copy.bis: Ang init, hangin, kahayag, ug moisture makadaot sa mga tambal ug maghimo niini nga dili kaayo epektibo o dili luwas imnon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Heat energy can cook food, melt ice, and warm a room
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes everyday effects of heat energy (cooking, melting, warming) and heat transfer from warm to cool places. G10-F-9 requires describing high voltage electricity generation and safe distribution from power plants, including substations and electric meters. The card provides no information about electricity generation, transmission, or distribution, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
What changes can heat energy cause?

Heat energy can cook food, melt ice, and warm a room, because it moves from warm places to cool places!
copy.tl:
Anong mga pagbabago ang maaaring idulot ng heat energy?

Ang heat energy ay maaaring magluto ng pagkain, magpatunaw ng yelo, at magpainit ng silid, dahil gumagalaw ito mula sa mainit na lugar papunta sa malamig na lugar!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga kausaban ang mahimo sa heat energy?

Ang heat energy makaluto og pagkaon, makapatunaw sa yelo, ug makapainit sa kwarto, tungod kay molihok kini og init nga lugar ngadto sa bugnaw nga lugar!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Adding heat to a system increases its internal energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of covalent bonds using a molecule of water and a molecule of carbon dioxide
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses heat and internal energy, which is a physics/thermodynamics concept. G9-M-7 requires explaining covalent bond formation using water and carbon dioxide molecules; the card provides no information about chemical bonding, molecules, or covalent bonds.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Adding heat to a system increases its internal energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: G7-M-8 requires identifying the roles of solute and solvent in a solution. The card is about heat increasing internal energy and contains nothing about solutions, solutes, or solvents.

copy.en: Adding heat to a system increases its internal energy, the total energy stored inside all its particles.
copy.tl: Ang pagdagdag ng init sa isang system ay nagpapataas ng internal energy nito, ang kabuuang enerhiyang nakaimbak sa loob ng lahat ng particle nito.
copy.bis: Ang pagdugang og init sa usa ka system mopataas sa internal energy, ang tibuok nga enerhiya nga gitipigan sa tanang particle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Use heat-resistant gloves or tongs when handling hot equipment to prevent burns from hot surfaces or glassware.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about laboratory safety when handling hot equipment. G10-E-6 requires explaining how subduction of an oceanic plate impacts the plate above it, a plate tectonics concept. There is no connection to subduction, oceanic plates, or plate interactions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Use heat-resistant gloves or tongs when handling hot equipment to prevent burns from hot surfaces or glassware.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the location and distribution of active volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, and major mountain belts to the distribution of oceanic crust and continental crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about using heat-resistant gloves to prevent burns. G8-E-5 requires relating the distribution of volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, and mountain belts to oceanic and continental crust. The card provides no information about crustal distribution or geological features.

copy.en: Use heat-resistant gloves or tongs when handling hot equipment to prevent burns from hot surfaces or glassware.
copy.tl: Gumamit ng heat-resistant gloves o tongs kapag humahawak ng mainit na equipment upang maiwasan ang paso mula sa mainit na surface o glassware.
copy.bis: Gamita ang heat-resistant gloves o tongs kon maggunit og init nga equipment aron malikayan ang paso gikan sa init nga surface o glassware.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When you heat a solid such as ice, its temperature rises first because the particles move faster and vibrate more before the solid changes state.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate and describe the relationship among the projectile variables including the angle and velocity of release, and projectile height and range, using everyday activities such as shooting basketballs or kicking footballs
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses heating a solid and particle motion before a state change, which is unrelated to projectile motion variables (angle, velocity, height, range). The assigned competency is about projectile motion, so the tag is incorrect.

copy.en: When you heat a solid such as ice, its temperature rises first because the particles move faster and vibrate more before the solid changes state.
copy.tl: Kapag pinainit mo ang isang solid tulad ng yelo, tumataas muna ang temperature nito dahil bumibilis at dumadami ang vibration ng mga particle bago pa man magbago ng state ang solid.
copy.bis: Kon imong initon ang usa ka solid sama sa yelo, mosaka una ang temperature niini tungod kay mopaspas ug modaghan ang vibration sa mga particle sa dili pa mausab ang state sa solid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the average kinetic energy of its molecules increases
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains heating and molecular kinetic energy, which is physics/chemistry content. G9-L-6 requires classifying Philippine animals and plants as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species. There is no connection to biodiversity or species classification.

copy.en: When an object is heated, the average kinetic energy of its molecules increases, making them move faster and raising the object's temperature.
copy.tl: Kapag pinainit ang isang bagay, tumataas ang average na kinetic energy ng mga molecule nito, kaya mas mabilis silang gumagalaw at tumataas ang temperatura ng bagay.
copy.bis: Kung initon ang usa ka butang, mosaka ang average nga kinetic energy sa mga molecule, busa mas mopaspas sila sa paglihok ug mosaka ang temperatura sa butang.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The higher an object is lifted, the more potential energy it stores
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using flow charts and labeled diagrams explain the role of plants and animals in the cycles of nature, such as the carbon, oxygen, and water cycles
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about gravitational potential energy and height, a physics topic. Why don't hormone levels go crazy during the menstrual cycle?

Ngano man nga dili magkagubot ang lebel sa mga hormone panahon sa menstrual cycle?

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the difference between a vaccine and deworming medicine, focusing on the immune system and intestinal worms. It does not describe the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems as required by G4-L-1.

copy.en:
What's the difference between a vaccine and deworming medicine?

A vaccine teaches your immune system to fight germs that cause disease, while deworming medicine just kills worms in your gut — it doesn't teach any defense!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng bakuna at purga?

Ang bakuna ay nagtuturo sa immune system laban sa mga germ na sanhi ng sakit, samantalang ang purga ay gamot lang na pumapatay sa mga bulate sa tiyan — hindi ito nagtuturo ng depensa!
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa bakuna ug purga?

Ang bakuna nagtudlo sa immune system batok sa mga germ nga hinungdan sa sakit, samtang ang purga usa ra ka tambal nga mopatay sa mga ulod sa tiyan — dili kini magtudlo og depensa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Blood flow delivers oxygen, provides nutrients, removes waste, maintains body temperature, and fights infection!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the properties of ionic, covalent, and metallic substances, such as melting point, hardness, electrical and thermal conductivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the importance of blood flow in the body, a biology topic. copy.en:
Why is blood flow important for the body?

Blood flow delivers oxygen, provides nutrients, removes waste, maintains body temperature, and fights infection!
copy.tl:
Bakit mahalaga ang daloy ng dugo sa katawan?

Ang daloy ng dugo ay naghahatid ng oxygen, nagbibigay ng nutrients, nag-aalis ng waste, nagpapanatili ng temperatura ng katawan, at lumalaban sa infection!
copy.bis:
Ngano importante man ang pag-agos sa dugo sa lawas?

Ang pag-agos sa dugo naghatod ug oxygen, naghatag ug nutrients, nagtangtang ug waste, nagpabilin sa temperatura sa lawas, ug makig-away sa infection!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Improper use of fertilizers, pesticides, and insecticides destroys the quality of the soil, which is called soil pollution!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses soil pollution from fertilizer misuse, which is unrelated to the competency on guided investigations of light reflection and refraction using mirrors, lenses, and prisms.

copy.en:
Why does improper use of fertilizers cause soil pollution?

Improper use of fertilizers, pesticides, and insecticides destroys the quality of the soil, which is called soil pollution!
copy.tl:
Bakit nagdudulot ng soil pollution ang maling paggamit ng fertilizers?

Ang maling paggamit ng fertilizers, pesticides, at insecticides ay sumisira sa kalidad ng lupa, na tinatawag na soil pollution!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga ang sayop nga paggamit sa fertilizers makahatod ug soil pollution?

Ang sayop nga paggamit sa fertilizers, pesticides, ug insecticides makaguba sa kalidad sa yuta, nga gitawag ug soil pollution!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the impulse-momentum theorem (force × time = change in momentum), which is a mechanics concept. assignedReviews.card_evidence: The impulse-momentum theorem states that force multiplied by time equals the change in momentum
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: collaborate in a class discussion to recognize the advantages and limitations of using series or parallel circuits
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about impulse and momentum, not about series or parallel circuits. G9-F-9 requires recognizing advantages and limitations of series/parallel circuits, which the card does not address at all.

copy.en: The impulse-momentum theorem states that force multiplied by time equals the change in momentum, so a longer stopping time means less force.
copy.tl: Ang impulse-momentum theorem ay nagsasabi na ang puwersa na minultiplika sa oras ay katumbas ng pagbabago sa momentum, kaya ang mas mahabang oras ng paghinto ay nangangahulugan ng mas maliit na puwersa.
copy.bis: Ang impulse-momentum theorem nag-ingon nga ang puwersa nga gipadaghan sa oras katumbas sa pagbag-o sa momentum, busa ang mas taas nga oras sa paghunong nagpasabot ug mas gamay nga puwersa.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes inactive volcanoes, a geology/earth science topic. G4-M-3 is about chemical properties of materials (burning, reactivity, degradability). There is no instructional support for chemical properties of materials.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes inactive volcanoes, which is unrelated to proper handling and disposal of materials (reusing, recycling, disposing of oil). No connection to the competency's content.

copy.en: An inactive volcano has not erupted for the last 10,000 years, and its shape is slowly being changed by weathering and erosion, forming deep gullies.
copy.tl: Ang isang inactive na bulkan ay hindi pumutok sa huling 10,000 taon, at ang hugis nito ay dahan-dahang nababago ng weathering at erosion, na bumubuo ng malalalim na gullies.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka inactive nga bulkan wala mibuto sa milabay nga 10,000 ka tuig, ug ang porma niini hinay-hinay nga nausab tungod sa weathering ug erosion, nga nagporma ug lawom nga mga gullies.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain what volcanoes are and how they are formed
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the concept of an independent variable in experiments. It has no content about volcanoes, their formation, or volcanic activity, so it does not support G6-E-1.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about experimental variables, not about materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines. It is unrelated to G6-E-4.

copy.en:
What is the independent variable in an experiment?

It is the one thing you deliberately change or control, like the amount of salt you add to water.
copy.tl:
Ano ang independent variable sa isang experiment?

Ito ang isang bagay na sadya mong binabago o kinokontrol, tulad ng dami ng asin na idinaragdag mo sa tubig.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang independent variable sa usa ka experiment?

Kini ang usa ka butang nga gituyo nimo nga usbon o kontrolon, sama sa gidaghanon sa asin nga imong idugang sa tubig.

copy.en: Indirect evidence for evolution comes from comparing structures like homologous, analogous, and vestigial body parts, where scientists infer change without watching it happen.
copy.tl: Ang indirect evidence para sa ebolusyon ay nagmumula sa paghahambing ng mga bahagi ng katawan tulad ng homologous, analogous, at vestigial structures, kung saan hinihinuha ng mga scientist ang pagbabago kahit hindi nila ito direktang nakikita.
copy.bis: Ang indirect evidence alang sa ebolusyon naggikan sa pagkumpara sa mga parte sa lawas sama sa homologous, analogous, ug vestigial structures, diin ang mga scientist maghinapos sa pag-usab bisan wala nila kini direktang nakita.

copy.tl: Ang infrasonic sounds ay may pitch na masyadong mababa para marinig ng tenga ng tao, kahit na may mga hayop na nakakarinig nito.
copy.bis: Ang infrasonic sounds adunay pitch nga hilabihan ka ubos aron madungog sa dalunggan sa tao, bisan pa nga adunay mga mananap nga makadungog niini.

copy.tl: Ang mga bata ay maaaring magmana ng mental abilities, talino, at talento mula sa magulang, ngunit kailangan ng tamang pagsasanay para malinang ang mga ito.
copy.bis: Ang mga bata mahimong makapanunod ug mental abilities, kaalam, ug talento gikan sa ginikanan, apan kinahanglan ug saktong pagbansay aron molambo kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deep in your ear are three tiny curved tubes filled with fluid.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency G4-L-1 covers the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The card describes the inner ear's semicircular canals and balance, which is part of the sensory/nervous system and is not one of the listed body systems. It provides no instructional support for any of the five systems named in the competency.

copy.en:
What tells your brain you're balanced?

Deep in your ear are three tiny curved tubes filled with fluid. When your head turns, the fluid moves and tells your brain about your balance and body position.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagsasabi sa utak kung balanse ka?

Malalim sa tenga mo ay may tatlong maliit na hubog na tubo na may likido. Kapag lumiko ang ulo mo, gumagalaw ang likido at nagbibigay-alam sa utak tungkol sa balanse at posisyon ng katawan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagsulti sa utak nga naa ka balanse?

Lawom sa dalunggan naa ang tulo ka gagmayng liko nga tubo nga adunay likido. Kon motiko ang imong ulo, molihok ang likido ug mopahibalo sa utak bahin sa balanse ug posisyon sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Internal energy is the total energy inside an object
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary resources to classify animals and plants of the Philippines as critically endangered, endangered, or vulnerable species
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains internal energy, a physics concept, and provides no information about classifying Philippine animals or plants as endangered species. It is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Internal energy is the total energy inside an object, including the kinetic energy of all its moving particles and the potential energy from how those particles interact.
copy.tl: Ang internal energy ay ang kabuuang energy sa loob ng isang bagay, kasama ang kinetic energy ng lahat ng gumagalaw na particle nito at ang potential energy mula sa interaksyon ng mga particle na iyon.
copy.bis: Ang internal energy mao ang kinatibuk-ang energy sa sulod sa usa ka butang, lakip ang kinetic energy sa tanang naglihok nga particle ug ang potential energy sa interaksyon sa mga particle.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are split into tiny chunks called packets that take different paths and are reassembled at the other end.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify practical applications of electromagnetic radiation, such as radio waves used in telecommunications, and x-rays and gamma rays in medicine
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes internet packet transmission, not electromagnetic radiation or its practical applications such as radio waves, x-rays, or gamma rays. No connection to the competency's subject.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They are split into tiny chunks called packets that take different paths and are reassembled at the other end.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and describe some ways to use movement, sound, and light to send information between two people
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about digital internet packets, not about using movement, sound, or light to send information between two people. It does not support the guided activities described in the competency.

copy.en:
How do messages travel on the internet?

They don't travel in one piece! They are split into tiny chunks called packets that take different paths and are reassembled at the other end.
copy.tl:
Paano naglalakbay ang mga mensahe sa internet?

Hindi sila dumadaan nang buo! Pinaghihiwalay sila sa maliliit na piraso na tinatawag na packets, na maaaring mag-iba ng daan, at pinagsasama uli sa dulo.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagbiyahe sa mga mensahe sa internet?

Dili kini molabay nga tibuok! Gibahinbahin kini sa gagmay nga bahin nga gitawag ug packets, nga mahimong magkalainlain ug agianan, ug gisumpay-sumpay balik sa tumoy.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses inventions that make work easier, with no mention of particle arrangement, spacing, or motion in states of matter. It does not support the competency at all.

copy.en: Scientists invent materials that make our work easier and faster, like tools and products we use at home, in school, and in our community.
copy.tl: Ang mga scientist ay nag-iimbento ng mga materyales na nagpapadali at nagpapabilis sa ating trabaho, tulad ng mga gamit at produktong ginagamit natin sa bahay, paaralan, at komunidad.
copy.bis: Ang mga scientist nag-imbento og mga materyales nga makapasayon ug makapadali sa atong trabaho, sama sa mga gamit ug produkto nga atong ginagamit sa balay, eskwelahan, ug komunidad.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses iodine's role in fetal brain development, which is unrelated to identifying basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not support the competency's content.

copy.en: Iodine is important for pregnant mothers because it helps the baby's brain develop.
copy.tl: Mahalaga ang iodine sa mga buntis dahil tumutulong ito sa pag-unlad ng utak ng sanggol.
copy.bis: Importante ang iodine sa mga mabdos kay makatabang kini sa pag-uswag sa utok sa bata.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: first ionization energy decreases from top to bottom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ionization energy trends in the periodic table, which is chemistry content unrelated to simple machines (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys) required by G6-F-2.

copy.en:
Why is it easier to remove an electron from elements lower in a group?

Because the outer electron is farther from the nucleus, so first ionization energy decreases from top to bottom!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling tanggalin ang electron sa mga elementong nasa ibaba ng isang group?

Dahil mas malayo ang outer electron sa nucleus, kaya bumababa ang first ionization energy mula itaas pababa!
copy.bis:
Ngano mas sayon tangtangon ang electron sa mga elemento nga naa sa ubos sa usa ka group?

Tungod kay mas layo ang outer electron sa nucleus, mao nga mous-os ang first ionization energy gikan sa taas paubos!

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses astronaut crew rotation on the ISS, not modern research about celestial objects using telescopes and space probes. No direct or prerequisite support for the competency.

copy.en:
How long do astronauts usually stay on the ISS?

They live there for several months until a new crew arrives by rocket to replace them!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal karaniwang nakatira ang mga astronaut sa ISS?

Nakatira sila nang ilang buwan hanggang dumating ang bagong crew sa rocket para palitan sila!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay kasagaran magpuyo ang mga astronaut sa ISS?

Magpuyo sila sulod sa pipila ka bulan hangtud nga moabot ang bag-ong crew sa rocket aron mopuli kanila!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the International Space Station, an artificial satellite, and does not describe the general structure of the solar system, major celestial objects, or their features and composition.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the International Space Station, not natural objects seen in the sky such as the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars.

copy.en: Many nations built and run the International Space Station together, where astronauts live while it orbits Earth!
copy.tl: Maraming bansa ang nagtayo at nagpapatakbo ng International Space Station, kung saan nakatira ang mga astronaut habang umiikot sa Earth!
copy.bis: Daghang nasod ang nagtukod ug nagpadagan sa International Space Station, diin nagpuyo ang mga astronaut samtang naglibot kini sa Earth!

copy.tl: Unang tumubo ang langka sa mga bansa sa Timog Asya tulad ng India, bago ito kumalat sa Pilipinas!
copy.bis: Una nga mitubo ang nangka sa mga nasod sa Habagatang Asya sama sa India, una pa kini mikaylap sa Pilipinas!

copy.bis: Ang renewable energy sources mas labor-intensive kaysa non-renewable sources, nagpasabot nga mas daghan sila ug mahimo nga trabaho para sa mga tao sa komunidad.

copy.tl: Ang unit ng mechanical energy ay joule! Ang isang joule ay halos kasing-dami ng energy para maiangat ang isang maliit na mansanas ng isang metro.
copy.bis: Ang unit sa mechanical energy kay joule! Usa ka joule halos sama sa energy nga gikinahanglan aron maalsa ang usa ka gamay nga mansanas og usa ka metro.

copy.tl: Ang Jupiter ay natatakpan ng mga ulap na gawa sa ammonia crystals at posibleng ammonium hydrosulfide.
copy.bis: Ang Jupiter gitabonan sa mga panganod nga hinimo sa ammonia crystals ug posible nga ammonium hydrosulfide.
